title: Flex’s Axiom Raises $2B as It Prepares to Spin Off as an AI Power Infrastructure Company
key_facts: Funds affiliated with General Catalyst and Koch Equity Development agreed to buy $2.0 billion of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock in Axiom Solutions International.
The investment values Axiom at an initial enterprise value of $37.5 billion.
Axiom is the name of Flex's Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment once it separates; Flex intends to spin it off as a public company in the first quarter of calendar 2027.
Proceeds will help fund Axiom's pending $4.4 billion acquisition of EPC Power, repay bridge financing, pay preferred dividends and general purposes.
The preferred stock pays a 10% annual cash dividend before the separation, then 6% in cash or 7% if paid in kind.
EPC Power makes power conversion equipment for data centers, energy storage and microgrids, with more than 15 gigawatts deployed in 62 countries.
Flex CEO Revathi Advaithi is expected to lead Axiom, which will compete with Vertiv, Schneider Electric and Eaton.
quote_evidence: Flex announced that funds affiliated with General Catalyst and Koch Equity Development (Koch Industries’ private equity arm), along with co-investors, agreed to buy $2.0 billion of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock in Axiom.
The investment values Axiom at an initial enterprise value of $37.5 billion.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows large private capital going into the power and cooling equipment that AI data centers need, via a corporate spin-off rather than a startup round.
event_date: Announced by Flex around 9-10 Oct 2026 (article dated 10 Oct)
notes: Wowtale relays Flex's announcement; the Flex press release itself was not opened. Wowtale links the item to Oxide and other rounds as context only.
